item.title: The OSSD, explained: what the diploma actually asks for
item.description: Thirty credits, forty hours, one literacy requirement. Once you can see the pieces, the Ontario Secondary School Diploma stops feeling like a maze and starts looking like a map.

item.title: A Parent's Guide to Online Learning
item.description: When your child learns online, the school day happens in your home. This small guide is about the job parents actually hold in that day: set the stage, check in like a coach, and know where the help lives.

item.title: Meet the Guidance Counsellor Hub
item.description: Every student has questions that are not about coursework. Choosing courses, applying to university, scholarships, study permits and student life now have a home of their own in Canvas, the Bronston Guidance Counsellor Hub.

item.title: Press Play, Then Prove It: New Interactive Videos and Formative Checks
item.description: Our courses are changing in a way you can feel. Bronston made interactive videos now sit right beside the teacher lessons, with quick questions as you watch, and formative checks that help you know you are ready before you move on.

item.title: The Four-Week Reset: Getting Ready for September
item.description: Four weeks, four small things: walking your sleep back, the tech check nobody does until it's 8:58, and a soft launch week — from whichever time zone you're in.

item.title: Study Buddy, Not Ghostwriter: Using AI the Smart Way
item.description: AI as a study tool, not a shortcut — the honest rules, the best legitimate uses, and how to find the Bronston AI Tutor on our virtual courses site.

item.title: Bronston, But Make It Summer
item.description: The off-season edition: group chats that never sleep, an August camp for students touching down from overseas, and the great September question.
